biography: Juliano Taschetto, a name rapidly gaining traction in Brazilian motorsports, hails from the dusty karting tracks of Rio Grande do Sul. Born into a family with gasoline in their veins – his grandfather ran a small auto repair shop – Juliano's obsession with speed ignited early. He began karting at the age of 10, quickly displaying a raw, untamed talent that both thrilled and terrified his early coaches. His defining moment came during the 2016 Brazilian Karting Championship, where a daring last-lap overtake secured him the title, a victory that caught the eye of Gol Classic B team manager, Ricardo Oliveira. Since joining Gol Classic B, Juliano has been steadily honing his skills, proving to be a tenacious competitor, though sometimes prone to over-aggression. While still considered a rising star, his performances show great promise, and many believe he has the potential to reach the highest echelons of motorsport.
drivingStyle: Taschetto's driving style is characterized by relentless aggression and a never-say-die attitude. He attacks corners with unwavering commitment, often pushing the limits of grip and control. Tire management is still a work in progress, a consequence of his aggressive corner entry speeds. Under pressure, Juliano tends to become even more assertive, sometimes leading to risky maneuvers, but also to spectacular overtakes that solidify his reputation as a thrilling driver to watch.

rivalries.reason: A long-standing rivalry from their karting days. Vargas has always been seen as the polished, technically perfect driver, a direct contrast to Taschetto's raw aggression, leading to frequent on-track clashes.

The rivalry ignited after a controversial incident at Interlagos where Juliano's aggressive move forced Monteiro off the track, costing her valuable championship points. Monteiro has publicly criticized Taschetto's driving as reckless and dangerous.

Fonseca is Juliano's teammate at Gol Classic B. While there's respect, the internal competition to be the team's top driver has created tension, especially as both vie for the same opportunities and resources.

quirks: Always wears the same lucky pair of socks, gifted to him by his grandmother, for every race.
Before each race, he listens to a specific Brazilian folk song, believing it brings him good fortune.
He meticulously polishes his helmet visor before every session, claiming it helps him 'see the track clearer'.
famousQuote: "You either go all in, or you don't go at all. Second place is just the first loser."
careerHighlight: Winning the 2016 Brazilian Karting Championship with a stunning last-lap overtake, cementing his reputation as a driver with immense potential and unwavering determination.
careerLowPoint: Crashing out of the lead at the 2022 Curitiba Grand Prix due to over-aggression, costing him a potential breakthrough victory and severely damaging his team's chances in the championship.
